name: Marcus Aurelius: Notes to Self
note: Modern interpretations of the Meditations, written by Liza. Titles are short hooks for Shorts; briefs are the lessons. Import with: node scripts/import-video-topics.ts data-seed/video-topics/marcus-aurelius.json

topics.title: Master yourself before anything else
topics.brief: Master yourself before trying to master anything else. Before trying to control your surroundings, other people, or the direction of the world, learn to control your own thoughts, emotions, desires, and actions.

topics.title: You can't control life, only reactions
topics.brief: Control your reactions, even when you cannot control your circumstances. Life will constantly bring unexpected situations, disappointments, and difficulties, but you always have a choice in how you respond to them.

topics.title: Don't be a slave to pleasure
topics.brief: Never become a slave to temporary pleasures. Enjoy the good things in life, but don't allow food, entertainment, comfort, money, or other pleasures to control your decisions and weaken your discipline.

topics.title: Motivation is optional. Discipline isn't.
topics.brief: Do what needs to be done, even when you don't feel motivated. Discipline means understanding your responsibilities and fulfilling them regardless of your mood, energy, or desire to avoid difficult work.

topics.title: Pause before your emotions decide
topics.brief: Let reason guide your actions instead of temporary emotions. Before reacting to something that makes you angry, excited, jealous, or afraid, pause and consider what the wisest response would be.

topics.title: Never let anger shape who you are
topics.brief: Never allow anger to take control of your character. Someone else's behaviour may upset you, but losing your patience and behaving badly only allows their actions to influence the person you become.

topics.title: Strong people still feel fear
topics.brief: Train your mind to remain calm during difficult situations. A strong person is not someone who never experiences stress or fear, but someone who can think clearly and act wisely even when life becomes uncomfortable.

topics.title: Stop complaining that growth is hard
topics.brief: Stop complaining about the effort required to improve yourself. Personal growth demands sacrifice, patience, consistency, and uncomfortable decisions, so accept the process instead of constantly wishing it were easier.

topics.title: Your habits are building your future
topics.brief: Understand that your daily habits are slowly building your future. Every small decision you make repeatedly shapes your character, your abilities, your relationships, and ultimately the direction of your life.

topics.title: Be stronger than your excuses
topics.brief: Become stronger than your excuses. There will always be reasons to delay, avoid responsibility, or give up, but your future depends on whether you allow those excuses to dictate your actions.

topics.title: Your story about it hurts more
topics.brief: Much of your suffering comes from the way you interpret what happens to you. You cannot always prevent painful events, but you can learn not to make them worse through unnecessary negative thinking, assumptions, and imagined consequences.

topics.title: Hopeless? Try a different angle first
topics.brief: Change your perspective before deciding that your situation is hopeless. Sometimes the problem cannot immediately be changed, but looking at it differently can reveal opportunities, solutions, and lessons that you previously overlooked.

topics.title: What happened isn't what it means
topics.brief: Learn to separate what actually happened from the meaning you give it. Someone not responding to your message, losing an opportunity, or receiving criticism does not automatically mean you are worthless or that everything is going wrong.

topics.title: One bad moment, not a bad day
topics.brief: Don't allow negative thoughts to occupy your entire day. A difficult moment deserves your attention, but it does not deserve permission to control every other part of your life.

topics.title: Make your mind your ally
topics.brief: Make your mind your strongest ally rather than your greatest enemy. Develop the habit of encouraging yourself with reason, patience, and constructive thinking instead of constantly criticising yourself and imagining failure.

topics.title: Stop living in imaginary futures
topics.brief: Focus on reality instead of spending your energy worrying about imaginary futures. Prepare for what might happen when necessary, but don't allow possibilities that may never occur to steal the peace you could experience today.

topics.title: Don't invent problems that haven't happened
topics.brief: Stop creating additional problems through your imagination. Many situations are difficult enough without adding imagined rejection, embarrassment, failure, or disaster to something that has not even happened.

topics.title: See things as they are
topics.brief: See people and situations as they truly are, rather than as you wish they were. Accepting reality allows you to make wiser decisions instead of wasting your energy fighting against facts you refuse to acknowledge.

topics.title: You become what you keep thinking
topics.brief: Remember that the thoughts you repeatedly entertain gradually shape your character. If you constantly practise jealousy, resentment, fear, and bitterness, those qualities become familiar, but practising gratitude, courage, and patience strengthens them too.

topics.title: Guard what gets into your head
topics.brief: Protect your mind from unnecessary negativity and distractions. Be selective about what you listen to, what you watch, what conversations you participate in, and which thoughts you choose to entertain.

topics.title: Time is the one thing you can't recover
topics.brief: Never forget that your time on Earth is limited and cannot be recovered once it passes. Stop treating every day as if you have an unlimited supply of opportunities, because the time you waste today will never return.

topics.title: Stop postponing who you want to be
topics.brief: Stop postponing the person you want to become. If you want to become disciplined, knowledgeable, healthier, kinder, or more courageous, begin practising those qualities now rather than waiting for the perfect moment.

topics.title: Don't chase things that won't last
topics.brief: Don't spend your limited life chasing things that have no lasting importance. Wealth, popularity, possessions, and recognition may provide temporary satisfaction, but they cannot replace a life built around purpose, character, and meaningful relationships.

topics.title: Tomorrow is never guaranteed
topics.brief: Live today with the awareness that tomorrow is never guaranteed. This does not mean living recklessly, but recognising that ordinary moments are valuable and that important things should not always be postponed.

topics.title: Comparison steals time from your growth
topics.brief: Every moment spent unnecessarily comparing yourself with others is time taken away from improving your own life. Instead of measuring your progress against someone else's achievements, focus on becoming a better version of yourself.

topics.title: Let mortality wake you up
topics.brief: Do not spend your entire life fearing death, because death is part of the natural process of existence. Use the awareness of mortality as a reason to live meaningfully rather than allowing fear to prevent you from living fully.

topics.title: You don't need more time
topics.brief: You may not need more time as much as you need to use the time you already have more wisely. Learn to recognise distractions, unnecessary commitments, and habits that consume your days without contributing anything valuable.

topics.title: Your life is happening right now
topics.brief: Don't sacrifice the present moment by constantly worrying about what the future might bring. Plan responsibly for tomorrow, but remember that your life is actually being lived in the moments you are experiencing right now.

topics.title: You can't please everyone. Stop trying.
topics.brief: Stop wasting your life trying to satisfy everyone's expectations. You have limited time and energy, so use them to become someone you respect rather than spending your entire existence seeking approval from other people.

topics.title: Was today worth the time?
topics.brief: Make your actions worthy of the time you have been given. At the end of each day, consider whether you used your time to learn, contribute, improve, and live according to your principles.

topics.title: Everyone is fighting a hidden battle
topics.brief: Be patient with people because everyone is fighting battles that you may know nothing about. Not everyone will behave perfectly, understand your perspective, or respond with kindness, so try to approach human imperfections with patience and understanding.

topics.title: Not everyone thinks like you
topics.brief: Don't expect everyone to think, behave, or make decisions the way you do. Every person has different experiences, knowledge, values, and weaknesses, and accepting these differences will save you from unnecessary frustration.

topics.title: Don't become what hurt you
topics.brief: When someone behaves badly toward you, don't allow their behaviour to turn you into someone you are not. You cannot always control how people treat you, but you can protect your integrity by refusing to imitate their dishonesty, cruelty, or ignorance.

topics.title: Meet ignorance with understanding, not anger
topics.brief: Respond to ignorance with understanding instead of immediately choosing anger. People sometimes act badly because they lack knowledge, self-awareness, or good judgment, and remembering this can help you respond more wisely.

topics.title: Revenge keeps you chained to them
topics.brief: Don't waste your life seeking revenge against people who have wronged you. Revenge keeps your mind attached to the person and the incident, whereas moving forward allows you to reclaim your attention and energy.

topics.title: Be fair when nobody's keeping score
topics.brief: Treat others fairly, even when there is nothing to gain from doing so. Your integrity is demonstrated most clearly when you choose to do what is right without expecting rewards, recognition, or personal benefits.

topics.title: Their behaviour doesn't decide your character
topics.brief: Never give another person's behaviour the power to determine your own character. Someone else's dishonesty does not justify yours, their anger does not require your anger, and their disrespect does not require you to abandon your principles.

topics.title: Help without keeping a tally
topics.brief: Help people without constantly calculating what you will receive in return. Genuine kindness comes from understanding that cooperation and contribution are valuable in themselves, not simply tools for gaining favours.

topics.title: Listen first, judge later
topics.brief: Listen carefully before judging someone else's words or actions. You may discover that there is more to their situation than you initially understood, and learning to listen can prevent unnecessary conflict.

topics.title: People aren't your competition
topics.brief: Remember that human beings are meant to live and work together. Instead of viewing everyone as competition, recognise that cooperation, mutual respect, and helping one another are essential parts of a meaningful society.

topics.title: The obstacle is your training
topics.brief: An obstacle can become an opportunity to develop qualities you would never discover through an easy life. Difficult circumstances can teach you patience, courage, creativity, endurance, and the ability to solve problems.

topics.title: Character shows when plans fall apart
topics.brief: Your character becomes more visible when life stops going according to your plans. It is easy to appear patient and confident when everything is comfortable, but true strength is demonstrated when circumstances test your principles.

topics.title: Stop running from every hard thing
topics.brief: Don't automatically run away from every difficult situation. Some challenges are necessary for personal growth, and avoiding every uncomfortable experience can prevent you from developing the strength and wisdom you need.

topics.title: Yesterday is done. What's next?
topics.brief: Accept what has already happened and direct your energy toward what you can do next. You cannot reverse yesterday's mistakes or decisions, but you can learn from them and make better choices moving forward.

topics.title: Let hardship make you better, not bitter
topics.brief: Hardship can strengthen your character when you respond to it with courage and wisdom. Rather than allowing suffering to make you bitter, use difficult experiences to develop greater patience, understanding, and resilience.

topics.title: Stay steady when life gets chaotic
topics.brief: Remain steady when life becomes unpredictable. You may not be able to control changing circumstances, financial uncertainty, disappointment, or unexpected losses, but you can practise maintaining a clear and disciplined mind.

topics.title: One failure doesn't define you
topics.brief: Never allow one failure to convince you that you are incapable of succeeding. A failed attempt is an experience from which you can learn, not a permanent definition of your intelligence, abilities, or potential.

topics.title: Every bad day is practice
topics.brief: Every difficult situation gives you an opportunity to practise virtue. Frustration gives you an opportunity to practise patience, fear gives you an opportunity to practise courage, and temptation gives you an opportunity to practise self-control.

topics.title: Don't wish for easier. Get stronger.
topics.brief: Instead of constantly wishing that life were easier, work on becoming wiser and stronger. You cannot remove every challenge from your path, but you can develop the qualities necessary to face those challenges more effectively.

topics.title: Stay strong without going cold
topics.brief: Endure hardship without allowing it to destroy your kindness and humanity. Strength does not mean becoming cold, cruel, or emotionally disconnected; it means remaining principled even when life gives you reasons to become bitter.

topics.title: You're not more important than anyone
topics.brief: Never convince yourself that you are more important than everyone around you. Regardless of your wealth, education, position, or achievements, you remain a human being who is equally subject to life's uncertainties and limitations.

topics.title: Your worth isn't measured in praise
topics.brief: Stop depending on praise from people to determine your self-worth. Compliments and recognition may feel good, but your sense of value should come from your character, decisions, and the principles you follow.

topics.title: Fame fades. Character doesn't.
topics.brief: Remember that public recognition is temporary, while the quality of your character matters in every moment. People may remember your achievements for a while, but the way you live and treat others is what truly defines you.

topics.title: Admit you're wrong, then learn
topics.brief: Be humble enough to admit when you are wrong and wise enough to learn from it. Defending every mistake simply to protect your ego prevents you from growing into a more knowledgeable and reasonable person.

topics.title: Don't let success go to your head
topics.brief: Don't allow success to make you arrogant or disrespectful toward others. Achievements should encourage gratitude and responsibility, not create the belief that you are superior to people who have achieved less.

topics.title: Take the lesson, leave the insult
topics.brief: Learn to receive criticism without allowing it to destroy your confidence. Consider whether the criticism contains something useful, accept what can help you improve, and refuse to let meaningless insults control your emotions.

topics.title: You don't owe anyone proof
topics.brief: You don't need to spend your life proving your worth to everyone you meet. Focus on developing genuine abilities and good character rather than constantly trying to convince other people that you are successful or important.

topics.title: Be good, don't just look good
topics.brief: Be more concerned with becoming a good person than appearing to be one. There is a significant difference between genuinely practising honesty, kindness, and discipline and simply creating an image that makes other people admire you.

topics.title: Emperors die too
topics.brief: Remember that everyone is mortal, regardless of their wealth, power, or social position. No amount of influence or achievement makes someone permanently superior to the natural realities that every human being eventually faces.

topics.title: Show it, don't announce it
topics.brief: Let your actions demonstrate your character instead of constantly talking about your qualities. A person who genuinely possesses discipline, wisdom, and integrity does not need to repeatedly announce those qualities to the world.

topics.title: Wake up with a purpose
topics.brief: Begin each morning by remembering that you have responsibilities and opportunities to contribute something meaningful. Don't approach the day only thinking about comfort and entertainment; consider what useful work you can accomplish.

topics.title: Do great work when nobody's watching
topics.brief: Do your work with excellence, even when nobody is watching or rewarding you. Your standards should come from your own principles rather than depending entirely on supervision, praise, or external recognition.

topics.title: Stop complaining about your responsibilities
topics.brief: Don't constantly complain about the responsibilities that are part of your life. If something genuinely needs to be done, approach it with discipline and understand that fulfilling your responsibilities is part of living with purpose.

topics.title: Just do the task in front of you
topics.brief: Give your complete attention to the task directly in front of you. Instead of becoming overwhelmed by everything you need to accomplish, concentrate on doing the present task properly before moving to the next one.

topics.title: Work for more than yourself
topics.brief: Work for the common good rather than focusing exclusively on your personal advantage. Your skills, knowledge, and efforts become more meaningful when they also contribute something useful to the lives of other people.

topics.title: Perfect conditions never come. Start now.
topics.brief: Don't wait for perfect circumstances before beginning something important. There will always be uncertainty, inconvenience, and reasons to delay, so learn to make progress with the resources and opportunities currently available.

topics.title: Be useful, not just impressive
topics.brief: Aim to become genuinely useful rather than simply impressive. Having a prestigious title or appearing successful matters less than developing abilities that solve problems and make a positive difference.

topics.title: Do fewer things, better
topics.brief: Avoid dividing your attention between too many unnecessary activities. Focus creates better work, clearer thinking, and greater progress than constantly jumping between distractions without completing anything meaningful.

topics.title: Let your work prove your values
topics.brief: Let your work reflect the values you claim to believe in. If you value honesty, responsibility, and excellence, demonstrate those qualities through the way you approach your everyday professional and personal responsibilities.

topics.title: Do right even without a reward
topics.brief: Do the right thing even when there is no immediate reward for doing it. Your principles should remain consistent whether people appreciate your efforts, criticise your decisions, or never even notice what you have done.

topics.title: The next thing won't make you happy
topics.brief: Understand that happiness does not require owning everything you desire. If you constantly believe that the next purchase, achievement, relationship, or financial milestone will finally make you happy, you may never learn to appreciate your present life.

topics.title: Notice what you already have
topics.brief: Develop the habit of appreciating what you already have instead of constantly focusing on what is missing. Gratitude helps you recognise the value of ordinary things that you might otherwise overlook while chasing bigger ambitions.

topics.title: You never see their whole story
topics.brief: Stop comparing your life with the lives of other people. You rarely know the full story behind another person's success, struggles, or circumstances, so comparing your progress with theirs is often unfair and unproductive.

topics.title: Want less, feel more peace
topics.brief: Understand that inner peace becomes easier when you learn to manage your desires. The more you depend on external achievements and possessions for satisfaction, the more opportunities you create for disappointment and dissatisfaction.

topics.title: Enjoy comfort, don't depend on it
topics.brief: Learn to live comfortably without becoming dependent on luxury. Enjoy good things when they are available, but develop enough self-sufficiency that losing temporary comforts does not destroy your sense of stability.

topics.title: Don't hand your peace to others
topics.brief: Don't make your peace of mind completely dependent on things outside your control. Other people's opinions, economic conditions, unexpected events, and changing circumstances should not have unlimited power over your inner stability.

topics.title: Know when you have enough
topics.brief: Learn to recognise when you have enough. Ambition can encourage growth, but endless wanting can prevent you from enjoying the progress, opportunities, and resources already present in your life.

topics.title: Life isn't a waiting room
topics.brief: Don't allow the pursuit of future success to destroy your ability to appreciate today. Work toward your goals, but remember that life is not simply a waiting room where happiness begins after you achieve something.

topics.title: Real fulfilment comes from your principles
topics.brief: Find fulfilment in living with honesty, justice, courage, and wisdom. External rewards can disappear or change, but living according to strong principles gives your life a deeper sense of meaning.

topics.title: Peace beats looking successful
topics.brief: Understand that a peaceful mind is more valuable than an impressive appearance. Having a life that looks successful to others means very little if you constantly experience jealousy, anxiety, dissatisfaction, and inner conflict.

topics.title: Never stop learning
topics.brief: Never stop learning simply because you have reached a certain age or level of success. There will always be something you don't understand, a weakness you can improve, or a perspective that can make you wiser.

topics.title: Question your first assumption
topics.brief: Question your assumptions before accepting them as facts. Your first interpretation of an event may be influenced by fear, ego, or incomplete information, so practise examining situations carefully before reaching conclusions.

topics.title: Choose truth over comfort
topics.brief: Choose truth over comfort, even when the truth challenges your existing beliefs. Personal growth requires the courage to recognise your mistakes, question your opinions, and change your understanding when better evidence becomes available.

topics.title: It's okay not to know
topics.brief: Be comfortable admitting that you don't know everything. Humility creates room for learning, while pretending to know everything prevents you from asking questions and discovering better ways to think.

topics.title: Learn from mistakes, don't hate yourself
topics.brief: Treat your mistakes as lessons rather than reasons to hate yourself. Reflect on what went wrong, understand which decisions contributed to the outcome, and use that knowledge to behave more wisely in the future.

topics.title: Think before you speak
topics.brief: Think carefully about your words before allowing them to leave your mouth. Words can create unnecessary conflict, damage relationships, and reveal poor judgment, so learn to speak with purpose, honesty, and consideration.

topics.title: Big decision? Let emotions cool first
topics.brief: Train yourself to think rationally before making important decisions. Strong emotions can influence your judgment, so take time to examine the facts, consider the consequences, and choose the action that best reflects your principles.

topics.title: Information isn't wisdom
topics.brief: Never confuse possessing information with possessing wisdom. Knowing many facts is useful, but wisdom comes from understanding how to apply knowledge responsibly in real situations.

topics.title: Three questions to end every day
topics.brief: Make time every day to reflect on your behaviour and decisions. Ask yourself where you acted well, where you allowed your emotions to control you, and what you could do differently tomorrow.

topics.title: Become someone you respect
topics.brief: Become the kind of person you genuinely respect. Instead of constantly admiring the qualities you see in others, begin practising those same qualities through your own decisions, habits, and behaviour.

topics.title: Control what you can. Accept the rest.
topics.brief: Accept what is outside your control and take responsibility for what remains within your control. You cannot command the world to follow your expectations, but you can choose your judgments, intentions, actions, and responses.

topics.title: Life doesn't owe you anything
topics.brief: Understand that life does not owe you comfort, success, or favourable circumstances. Accepting this reality helps you stop feeling personally offended whenever things become difficult or fail to happen according to your expectations.

topics.title: Everything is temporary. Enjoy it now.
topics.brief: Remember that everything in life is temporary and constantly changing. Relationships, possessions, achievements, emotions, and circumstances will eventually change, so appreciate them without expecting them to remain exactly as they are forever.

topics.title: Live by reason, not impulse
topics.brief: Try to live in harmony with reason, nature, and your responsibilities as a human being. Instead of being controlled by selfish desires or destructive impulses, aim to act thoughtfully and contribute positively to the world around you.

topics.title: Virtue over wealth, status and fame
topics.brief: Place virtue above wealth, status, pleasure, and reputation. These external things may improve your circumstances, but they cannot make you a genuinely good person if you lack honesty, justice, courage, and self-control.

topics.title: They can take everything except this
topics.brief: Protect your inner freedom by refusing to let external circumstances control your character. You may lose possessions, opportunities, comfort, or social approval, but you can still choose to remain honest, courageous, and principled.

topics.title: Stop fearing what's inevitable
topics.brief: Don't spend your life fearing things that are natural and inevitable. Ageing, change, uncertainty, and death are part of existence, and accepting them allows you to spend more energy living meaningfully.

topics.title: We're all one community
topics.brief: Treat every human being as part of one larger community. Your life is connected to the lives of others, so practise fairness, compassion, cooperation, and responsibility instead of behaving as though only your own interests matter.

topics.title: Don't let circumstances change who you are
topics.brief: Let your principles guide your decisions rather than allowing circumstances to change who you are. When you have established clear values, you can remain consistent even when doing the right thing becomes uncomfortable or unpopular.

topics.title: Did you live like your best self?
topics.brief: At the end of every day, ask yourself whether you lived according to the person you want to become. Examine your actions honestly, appreciate what you did well, recognise your weaknesses, and prepare to approach tomorrow with greater wisdom and discipline.
